name: Man City: the Big Five in £m
format: .pptx, PowerPoint default template, native line chart
setup: Board of a rival Premier League club. Decision: whether to raise a complaint that Man City's commercial revenue was out of line with its football record.
lead: Looking at the data from 2008/09 to 2024/25, Manchester City's commercial revenue increased from £18m to £340m, which is faster than Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United, all of whom grew more slowly over the period
tests: The classic first attempt: right numbers, wrong yardstick, no conclusion

faults.note: Describes growth; draws no conclusion for the board
Does not answer the board's question (revenue out of line with football record)
No football record on the chart, so it cannot show "out of line"
Absolute £m: league commercial revenue grew 5.6x and lifts every line
No index to the league average
Five rainbow lines; City not emphasised
Slide title is a topic, not the lead

right: Source line present; the lead's numbers can be read off the chart
question: With 12 faults on one page, which three should Daniel raise first, and should he stop there?

name: Man City: two aligned panels, overclaiming lead
setup: Board of a rival Premier League club. Decision: whether to raise a complaint that Man City's commercial revenue was out of line with its football record.
lead: Man City's sponsorship deals were inflated: its commercial revenue ran far ahead of its football record from 2009/10 to 2017/18
tests: A strong chart under a lead that claims more than it shows, with no number

faults.note: "Deals were inflated" claims wrongdoing; the chart shows revenue out of line with results, not why
The student's own footnote says "not why": the lead contradicts the chart

right: Indexed to the league average; all 13 clubs with data; 10-season average with a 5-season check; gaps not filled; City blue, others grey; two panels; log scale labelled; source and caveat
question: Should Daniel push for the connected scatter, since Man Utd's index tops City's in some seasons on this chart?

name: Kettle & Crumb: stacked columns for the station landlord
setup: Head of leasing at the rail-station landlord: 14 of Kettle & Crumb's 22 transit kiosks, all renewing in 2027. Decision: how hard to push Kettle & Crumb on renewal terms.
lead: Revenue growth 2023–26 by format: delivery kitchens fastest at 31% a year
tests: A true "what" that is the wrong conclusion for this client

faults.note: A what, not a so what
Wrong conclusion for the landlord: transit kiosks are the fastest-growing store format (HK$102m to HK$132m, +9% a year), so Kettle & Crumb needs these sites
Stacked columns bury the transit-kiosk trend in the middle of each bar
No emphasis on the series that matters
Labels on every segment plus a value axis plus a legend

right: Source line; units in the title
question: If the student is still stuck at round 3, should Daniel's offered lead name the transit kiosks?

name: Kestrel Pacific: 3D pie that echoes the CEO
setup: Group CEO, Kestrel Pacific Holdings (board, March 2026). Decision: how to split HK$2bn of capital across five businesses, 2026–30.
lead: Health & beauty retail is our biggest business at 37% of revenue, so it should get the most of the HK$2bn
tests: A non-sequitur lead that repeats the client's belief, plus a hard stop

faults.note: Repeats what the CEO already believes
Size does not justify capital: "so it should get the most" does not follow
Wrong measure for a capital decision: revenue share, not market attractiveness or position
Labels read "3100; 37%": no units, no separator

right: The lead's 37% is on the chart
question: A hard stop (no source) on a chart whose real problem is the logic: which does Daniel open with?

name: Northfield Footwear: the store P&L table
setup: VP Retail Operations, Northfield Footwear (12 US stores). Decision: which stores to close or remodel in 2027.
lead: Store profitability varies widely across the network and rents are rising too fast
tests: A data dump with a vague, two-part lead

faults.note: No rent trend in the data: "rising too fast" is unsupported
A 12 × 9 table where a ranked bar of contribution % would show the answer
Nothing marks the three loss-making stores

hidden: Springfield, Worcester and Albany lose US$156k a year combined; closing them lifts store contribution from US$808k to US$964k (+19%)
question: Should Daniel ever point at what the table actually shows (the three loss-makers), or only ask?

name: Lumen Optical: hand-drawn dummy waterfall
format: .jpg, phone photo of a pencil sketch
setup: CEO, Lumen Optical (45 eyewear stores in Hong Kong). Decision: which of three profit programmes to fund first in 2026.
lead: Three programmes lift EBIT by HK$35m to HK$90m by 2027, with pricing the biggest at HK$15m
tests: A good dummy chart with typos, a missing source and a wrong sum in the lead

faults.note: No source: where will each bar's data come from?
60 + 35 ≠ 90: the net gain after −5 inflation is 30

right: Waterfall is the right form; the lead's 15 and 90 are on the chart
question: D10 makes a wrong number in the lead Major: should it be a hard stop, like a typo? Is a photographed sketch an acceptable input?

name: Pearl River Packaging: the gap is buried
setup: CFO, Pearl River Packaging (Hong Kong-listed packaging maker). Decision: whether to push price increases in the 2026 customer contract round.
lead: Our margin per tonne has halved since 2021, from HK$1,200 to HK$600: push price rises in the 2026 contract round
tests: Single-issue test of the new rule: numbers in the lead must jump out

faults.note: HK$1,200 and HK$600 appear nowhere on the chart
The reader must subtract two lines to find the lead's numbers
Two levels on a 0–8,000 axis when the lead is about the gap: plot margin per tonne
Emphasis falls on price and cost, not the gap

right: Lead passes every L rule; class template, lead as title, subheading, source, no gridlines, direct labels
question: Is this one fault (plot the gap) or four? How should Daniel phrase it?

name: Aster & Moss: dual-axis screenshot
setup: CMO, Aster & Moss (Hong Kong skincare brand, online sales). Decision: whether to double the 2026 digital marketing budget.
lead: Sales took off once marketing spend passed HK$2m a month, so doubling the budget will double sales
tests: A causal claim built on a dual-axis crossing

faults.note: Dual axis: the "take-off" is where two arbitrary scales cross
Causal claim and a straight-line extrapolation from a correlation
Seasonality: sales also spiked in Nov–Dec 2024 at HK$1.4m spend; the 2025 jump is year-end
Not like-for-like: compare the same months year on year
Topic title ("Marketing Spend vs Online Sales")

right: Source given; units on both axes
question: How hard should Daniel push on the causal claim versus the chart mechanics?

name: Kaze Climate: strong chart, typos and an AI source
setup: Head of International, Kaze Climate (Japanese air-conditioner maker). Decision: which ASEAN market to enter first in 2027.
lead: Enter Vietnam first: its room air-conditioner market grows 9.8% a year to 2030, the fastest in ASEAN
tests: Hard stops on an otherwise strong page
right: Lead passes; sorted bars; Vietnam highlighted; 9.8% jumps out
possible: Growth alone may not justify entry without market size (D2): not seeded
question: After three hard stops, how much else should Daniel say? Does growth without market size deserve a comment?

name: Kestrel Pacific: portfolio map (control)
setup: Group CEO, Kestrel Pacific Holdings (board, March 2026). Decision: how to split HK$2bn of capital across five businesses, 2026–30.
lead: Put most of the HK$2bn into elderly care: our only business in an attractive market (4.6) where we are strong (4.7)
tests: Control: no seeded faults. Does Daniel invent problems?
possible: Cold-chain (attractive, weak) is left out of the lead; "4.6 / 4.7" relies on axis order
question: What is the one line on what works? Is anything here worth a comment at all?
